Subject: Regulated workload sizing request - Helix Production

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking this. We have an upcoming contract renewal and a planned migration of our clinical decision support pipeline into a managed inference environment. Given the regulatory constraints (PHI in a subset of requests, strict audit logging, and retention controls), we need a clear sizing and procurement recommendation: Dedicated reserved capacity vs private (VPC/on-prem) deployment.

Attached is a baseline capture of our production traffic (HelixProd_workload_baseline.xlsx) — peak TPS, token distributions, and the subset of PHI-tagged requests. High level: peak concurrent sessions ~120, 95th token length ~1,200, average request ~620 tokens.

Questions we need answered for the RFP:
- Cost delta (monthly) for dedicated reserved pool vs private deployment (ballpark).
- Lead times for procurement and onboarding.
- Recommended GPU types and counts for a two-year oltp+batch workload.
- How you recommend partitioning PHI vs non-PHI traffic (routing, isolation).

Can you get a preliminary recommendation by EOD Monday (2027-06-07)? Also copying Sanjay (infra) who will be our technical contact.

Best,

Subject: Internal: HelixPharma sizing scenarios (prelim)

Tessa / Rafael — quick notes from scenario runs against Marcus's baseline (see HelixProd_workload_baseline.xlsx). I left a copy of the detailed workbook (fleet-scenarios-v2.xlsx) in our folder. High-level takeaways: 

Workload assumptions (from baseline):
- 95th concurrency ~120 sessions, average tokens/request ~620, 95th tokens ~1,200.
- PHI traffic ~18% (sensitive path requires stricter key controls + audit retention).
- Latency SLO for interactive paths: p95 < 350ms for prompt+response tokenization; streaming allowed for long responses.

Scenarios considered:
A) Dedicated Reserved Pool (hosted)
 - Recommended mix: 6 x H100-80GB (primary pool) + 4 x A100-80GB (burst/quantized inference).
 - Rationale: H100 nodes for large-sequence low-latency (KV cache heavy). A100 for quantized, cost-efficient batch work.
 - Estimated throughput: ~18k tokens/s sustained; headroom for autoscale bursts to ~28k tokens/s with the A100 burst nodes.
 - Ballpark monthly cost (reserved pricing): USD $120k–$155k (includes instance reservation amortized + base infra).
 - Lead time: 8–12 weeks to provision reserved nodes in our dedicated rack + private-network peering.

B) Private (VPC-hosted / customer-managed)
 - Option 1: VPC-hosted (Redwood private control plane, customer VPC, Redwood-managed instances): 8 x A100-80GB (quantized profile) + 4 x H100 for PHI lanes.
 - Option 2: On-prem (customer buys hardware): recommendations same as above but capital procurement + integrator time.
 - Ballpark monthly OPEX + support (VPC): USD $140k–$165k (higher due to per-customer isolation, tooling, and extended observability).
 - On-prem CAPEX estimate (one-time): ~$1.2M–$1.6M for equivalent cluster (incl. rack, network, HSM/KMS appliances). Procurement & validation: 12–18 weeks.

Segregation strategy (recommended):
- Route PHI-tagged requests to an isolated lane with customer-managed KMS and dedicated audit exporters. Non-PHI requests go to the main shared pool or dedicated reserved pool depending on required SLO and cost constraints.
- For fastest time-to-value, propose: Dedicated Reserved pool for non-PHI; a small Private lane (VPC-hosted or on-prem) for PHI-only traffic. Traffic is routed by request-level metadata at the ingress.

Risk notes:
- Lead time for H100 procurement is the gating factor for on-prem solutions.
- A100 quantization may degrade some long-form output quality for specific models; recommend running Helix prompt set through both quantized and full-precision alpha to validate.

Next steps I recommend we present:
1) A single-slide recommendation (hosted Dedicated + small Private PHI lane) with costs & lead times.
2) A proposed rollout timeline (pilot 6–8 weeks, scale 12–16 weeks).
3) DocuSign for reserved contract (if they choose Dedicated) + procurement checklist for on-prem.

I'll pull together the single-slide and a tighter cost band for Monday's call.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: Recommendation: Hybrid approach (Dedicated reserved + PHI-private lane) — HelixPharma

Marcus / Sanjay — following our internal analysis and the items Vanessa summarized, here's a concise recommendation and the procurement path we suggest. TL;DR: choose Dedicated Reserved as the primary serving mode for fastest TTV and most predictable unit economics; add a small Private PHI lane (VPC-hosted or on-prem based on your preference) for sensitive requests.

Recommendation (concise):
- Primary: Dedicated Reserved pool (hosted) — 6 x H100-80GB nodes (primary, low-latency) + 4 x A100-80GB nodes for burst/quantized batch. This gives ~20–25% headroom over current peaks and keeps p95 latency comfortably under 350ms for interactive flows.
- PHI lane: VPC-hosted Private lane with 2 x H100-80GB and customer-managed KMS + dedicated audit exporters. This isolates keys, logs, and retention — satisfies most regulated audits without full on-prem CAPEX.

Costs & lead times (ballpark):
- Dedicated Reserved (monthly run rate, reserved amortized): USD $130k/month (range $120k–$155k). 8–12 week provisioning for reserved nodes + peering.
- Private PHI lane (VPC-hosted): USD $25k–$40k/month incremental (incl. networking, KMS, and additional observability).
- On-prem alternative: one-time CAPEX ~$1.2M–$1.6M, longer procurement 12–18 weeks + integration time.

Operational notes:
- Routing: request-level metadata at ingress will direct PHI to the private lane; non-PHI flows go to the dedicated pool. We'll provide the routing rules template and an ingress webhook you can host.
- Quality validation: we'll run your Helix prompt set against the quantized profiles and the full-precision H100 baseline to sign off on output parity.
- SLAs & rollback: Dedicated reserved comes with an SLA and fallback to compatible model variants in other regions. We'll include canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies in the onboarding plan.

Procurement & next steps:
1) Sign a short Statement of Work + Reserved Capacity commitment (DocuSign link: https://docusign.net/sign/ABCDEFG12345).
2) Select PHI lane preference (VPC-hosted vs on-prem). If VPC-hosted, we'll start peering & KMS setup immediately after SOW.
3) Pilot window (6–8 weeks) then scale to full footprint (additional 4–8 weeks).

If this aligns, can you confirm by Wed 06/16 so we can lock reserved node availability and start ordering? Happy to review line items on a call Monday 06/07 10:00am PT as suggested.

Thanks — looking forward to getting Helix into production.

Best,
